## Computing Summary Statistics
```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)
library(easystats)
library(knitr)
library(readxl)

df <- read_xlsx("Survey Data Set.xlsx") |> rename_with(trimws)

df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    `Preferred Deliverly Format` = recode(
      `Preferred Deliverly Format`,
      "PO" = "Primarily Online",
      "PI" = "Primarily In Person",
      "H"  = "Hybrid",
      "NP" = "No Preference"
    ),

    `Longer/Shorter Commute Time Effect on Preferred Lecture Format` =
      recode(
        `Longer/Shorter Commute Time Effect on Preferred Lecture Format`,
        "L;PO"  = "Longer; Primarily Online",
        "L;PI"  = "Longer; Primarily In Person",
        "L;H"   = "Longer; Hybrid",
        "L; H"  = "Longer; Hybrid",
        "S;PO"  = "Shorter; Primarily Online",
        "S;PI"  = "Shorter; Primarily In Person",
        "S; PI" = "Shorter; Primarily In Person",
        "S;H"   = "Shorter; Hybrid",
        "S; H"  = "Shorter; Hybrid",
        "No"    = "No effect"
      )
  )

quant_items <- c("Year of Study", "Benefit of Visual Learning", "Benefit of Hands On Learning", "Benefits of Auditory Learning", "Preferred Lecture Format Effectiveness", "Total Commute Time (Minutes)")

datawizard::describe_distribution(df, quant_items, centrality = c("mean", "median")) |>
  select(-Skewness, -Kurtosis, -n_Missing, -MAD) |>
  print_md()
m1_y = mean(df$`Year of Study`)
m2_y = median(df$`Year of Study`)
m3_y = sd(df$`Year of Study`)
m4_y = IQR(df$`Year of Study`)

m1_V = mean(df$`Benefit of Visual Learning`)
m2_V = median(df$`Benefit of Visual Learning`)
m3_V = sd(df$`Benefit of Visual Learning`)
m4_V = IQR(df$`Benefit of Visual Learning`)

m1_H = mean(df$`Benefit of Hands On Learning`)
m2_H = median(df$`Benefit of Hands On Learning`)
m3_H = sd(df$`Benefit of Hands On Learning`)
m4_H = IQR(df$`Benefit of Hands On Learning`)

m1_A = mean(df$`Benefits of Auditory Learning`)
m2_A = median(df$`Benefits of Auditory Learning`)
m3_A = sd(df$`Benefits of Auditory Learning`)
m4_A = IQR(df$`Benefits of Auditory Learning`)

m1_E = mean(df$`Preferred Lecture Format Effectiveness`)
m2_E = median(df$`Preferred Lecture Format Effectiveness`)
m3_E= sd(df$`Preferred Lecture Format Effectiveness`)
m4_E = IQR(df$`Preferred Lecture Format Effectiveness`)

m1_T = mean(df$`Total Commute Time (Minutes)`)
m2_T = median(df$`Total Commute Time (Minutes)`)
m3_T= sd(df$`Total Commute Time (Minutes)`)
m4_T = IQR(df$`Total Commute Time (Minutes)`)



summary_table = data.frame(check.names = FALSE, "Year of Study" = c(m1_y, m2_y, m3_y, m4_y),
                           "Benefit of Visual Learning" = c(m1_V, m2_V, m3_V, m4_V),
                           "Benefit of Hands On Learning" = c(m1_H, m2_H, m3_H, m4_H),
                           "Benefits of Auditory Learning" = c(m1_A, m2_A, m3_A, m4_A),
                   "Preferred Lecture Format Effectiveness" = c(m1_E, m2_E, m3_E, m4_E),
                   "Total Commute Time (Minutes)" = c(m1_T, m2_T, m3_T, m4_T))

kable(t(summary_table), 
      col.names = c("Mean", "Median", "SD", "IQR"), 
      caption = "Summary of Students' Preferences for Lecture Delivery Format",
      align = "c")



```
**Discussion for Quantitative Analysis**

We noticed that the mean for preferring visual & hands on learning are around the same
value while the medians are the same. However, the mean for preferring Auditory 
learning is significantly lower.

Additionally, we found that the standard deviation for total commute time is 
quite large.


 **qualitative variable**

```{r}
#| echo: false

datawizard::data_tabulate(df, c("Preferred Deliverly Format", "Longer/Shorter Commute Time Effect on Preferred Lecture Format")) |> print_md()

delF_dist = table(df$`Preferred Deliverly Format`)

ctime_dist = table(df$`Longer/Shorter Commute Time Effect on Preferred Lecture Format`)


delF_percent = prop.table(delF_dist) * 100
ctime_percent = prop.table(ctime_dist) * 100


delF_summary = rbind(
  Count = as.numeric(delF_dist),
  Percentage = as.numeric(delF_percent)
)

ctime_summary = rbind(
  Count = as.numeric(ctime_dist),
  Percentage = as.numeric(ctime_percent)
)


colnames(delF_summary) = names(delF_dist)
colnames(ctime_summary) = names(ctime_dist)

kable(delF_summary, caption = "Preferred Deliverly Format Responses")
      
kable(ctime_summary, caption = "Longer/Shorter Commute Time Effect on Preferred Lecture Format Responses")
```
**Discussion for the Qualitative Analysis**

For the preferred Delivery format we noticed that a large proportion of respondents 
prefer In-Person format.
We also noticed that a larger amount of respondents will change their preferred delivery format if they had shorter commute times. However, a lot of respondents reported that
their commute time would not affect their preferred delivery format.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 5
#| out-width: "95%"

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)

# Import the CSV file
data <- read_xlsx("Survey Data Set.xlsx") |> rename_with(trimws)

data <- data %>%
  mutate(
    `Preferred Deliverly Format` = recode(
      `Preferred Deliverly Format`,
      "PO" = "Primarily Online",
      "PI" = "Primarily In Person",
      "H"  = "Hybrid",
      "NP" = "No Preference"
    ),

    `Longer/Shorter Commute Time Effect on Preferred Lecture Format` =
      recode(
        `Longer/Shorter Commute Time Effect on Preferred Lecture Format`,
        "L;PO"  = "Longer; Primarily Online",
        "L;PI"  = "Longer; Primarily In Person",
        "L;H"   = "Longer; Hybrid",
        "L; H"  = "Longer; Hybrid",
        "S;PO"  = "Shorter; Primarily Online",
        "S;PI"  = "Shorter; Primarily In Person",
        "S; PI" = "Shorter; Primarily In Person",
        "S;H"   = "Shorter; Hybrid",
        "S; H"  = "Shorter; Hybrid",
        "No"    = "No effect"
      )
  )

# Check the column names
names(data)

# Create commute groups
data <- data %>%
  mutate(
    CommuteGroup = case_when(
        `Total Commute Time (Minutes)` > 40 ~ "Longer Commute",
        `Total Commute Time (Minutes)` < 40 ~ "Shorter Commute",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )

# Calculate proportions
proportions <- data %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(CommuteGroup),
    !is.na(`Preferred Deliverly Format`)
  ) %>%
  count(CommuteGroup, `Preferred Deliverly Format`) %>%
  group_by(CommuteGroup) %>%
  mutate(Proportion = n / sum(n)) %>%
  ungroup()

# Display the calculated proportions
print(proportions)

# Graph 1: Longer commutes
plot_longer <- ggplot(
  filter(proportions, CommuteGroup == "Longer Commute"),
  aes(x = `Preferred Deliverly Format`, y = Proportion)
) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  labs(
    title = "Preferred Delivery Format: Longer Commutes",
    x = "Preferred Delivery Format",
    y = "Proportion"
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::percent,
    limits = c(0, 1)
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(
    labels = c(
      "PO" = "Primarily Online",
      "PI" = "Primarily In Person",
      "H" = "Hybrid"
    )
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 30,
      hjust = 1,
      size = 9
    ),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 12),
    plot.margin = margin(10, 15, 15, 10)
  )

print(plot_longer)

# Graph 2: Shorter commutes
plot_shorter <- ggplot(
  filter(proportions, CommuteGroup == "Shorter Commute"),
  aes(x = `Preferred Deliverly Format`, y = Proportion)
) +
  geom_col(fill = "darkorange") +
  labs(
    title = "Preferred Delivery Format: Shorter Commutes",
    x = "Preferred Delivery Format",
    y = "Proportion"
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::percent,
    limits = c(0, 1)
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(
    labels = c(
      "PO" = "Primarily Online",
      "PI" = "Primarily In Person",
      "H" = "Hybrid"
    )
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 30,
      hjust = 1,
      size = 9
    ),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 12),
    plot.margin = margin(10, 15, 15, 10)
  )

print(plot_shorter)


```
**Discussion based on graph**
After doing a comparison of proportion statistical test, We found that 
respondents with longer (total commute time > Median) and 
shorter (total commute time < Median) both prefer In-person lectures.

**Comments on the linear Regression results**
After conducting the linear regression analysis, we can conclude that it is not 
an appropriate test for the data set because the y-axis (preferred delivery format)
is non-numerical. 

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig.width: 9
#| fig.height: 6
#| dpi: 300
#| fig-cap: "Checking the model assumptions of linear regression using the performance package."
library(tidyverse)
library(performance)

df <- read_xlsx("Survey Data Set.xlsx") |> rename_with(trimws)

df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    `Preferred Deliverly Format` = recode(
      `Preferred Deliverly Format`,
      "PO" = "Primarily Online",
      "PI" = "Primarily In Person",
      "H"  = "Hybrid",
      "NP" = "No Preference"
    ),

    `Longer/Shorter Commute Time Effect on Preferred Lecture Format` =
      recode(
        `Longer/Shorter Commute Time Effect on Preferred Lecture Format`,
        "L;PO"  = "Longer; Primarily Online",
        "L;PI"  = "Longer; Primarily In Person",
        "L;H"   = "Longer; Hybrid",
        "L; H"  = "Longer; Hybrid",
        "S;PO"  = "Shorter; Primarily Online",
        "S;PI"  = "Shorter; Primarily In Person",
        "S; PI" = "Shorter; Primarily In Person",
        "S;H"   = "Shorter; Hybrid",
        "S; H"  = "Shorter; Hybrid",
        "No"    = "No effect"
      )
  )

df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    `Benefit of Visual Learning` =
      as.numeric(as.character(`Benefit of Visual Learning`)),
    `Preferred Deliverly Format` =
      as.factor(`Preferred Deliverly Format`)
  )

# Fit the linear regression model
model <- lm(
  `Benefit of Visual Learning` ~ `Preferred Deliverly Format`,
  data = df
)

# View model results
summary(model)

# Check model assumptions
performance::check_model(model)
```

**Discussion on first Model assumptions**
Based on the results the linear regression model does not violate any of the
assumptions. However there is a dip in the homegeneity of Variance reference 
line and a few outliers in the Normality of Residuals.


```{r}

library(tidyverse)
library(performance)

df <- read_xlsx("Survey Data Set.xlsx") |> rename_with(trimws)


df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    `Benefit of Hands On Learning` =
      as.numeric(as.character(`Benefit of Hands On Learning`)),
    `Preferred Deliverly Format` =
      as.factor(`Preferred Deliverly Format`)
  )

# Fit the linear regression model
model <- lm(
  `Benefit of Hands On Learning` ~ `Preferred Deliverly Format`,
  data = df
)

# View model results
summary(model)

# Check model assumptions
performance::check_model(model)
```
**Discussion on Second Model assumptions**
Based on the results the linear regression model does not violate any of the
assumptions.  However, we noticed some outliers in the normality of residuals 
and a dip in the homogeneity of variance line.

```{r}
#| fig.width: 9
#| fig.height: 6
#| dpi: 300
library(tidyverse)
library(performance)

df <- read_xlsx("Survey Data Set.xlsx") |> rename_with(trimws)


df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    `Benefits of Auditory Learning` =
      as.numeric(as.character(`Benefits of Auditory Learning`)),
    `Preferred Deliverly Format` =
      as.factor(`Preferred Deliverly Format`)
  )

# Fit the linear regression model
model <- lm(
  `Benefits of Auditory Learning` ~ `Preferred Deliverly Format`,
  data = df
)

# View model results
summary(model)

# Check model assumptions
performance::check_model(model)
```
**Discussion on the third model assumption**
Based on the results the linear regression model does not violate any of the
assumptions. However, we noticed that the homogeneity of the variance line is not 
completely flat and there seems to be outliers in the normality of residuals. 

**Anova Table**
```{r}
library(tidyverse)

survey <- read_xlsx("Survey Data Set.xlsx") |> rename_with(trimws)

# Run a one-way ANOVA
anova_effectiveness <- aov(
  `Preferred Lecture Format Effectiveness` ~
    `Preferred Deliverly Format`,
  data = survey
)

# Display the ANOVA results
summary(anova_effectiveness)
```
**Discussion on the Anova Table**
Null Hypothesis (Ho: p >= 0.05): The mean lecture format effectiveness is equal across all preferred delivery format groups.
Alternative (Ha: p < 0.05): At least one groups mean effectiveness differs

Since P > 0.05 we fail to reject the Null Hypothesis.
